name: mechanical-doors-stream
purpose: One realistic multi-turn sitting that exercises the composer's mechanical doors — arithmetic fast-path plus its one deliberately-refused ambiguous case, widget build-and-iterate (judgment complaint, anaphoric complaint, and a definite-phrase complaint that hits the disclosed known-limitation fall-through to a new build), the second-person self-plane door, and an honest anaphoric-trap failure — woven into ordinary conversation rather than run as isolated command tests.

turns.user: hey — haven't opened this in a while, figured I'd actually sit down and use it properly tonight instead of just poking at it for two minutes and closing the tab.
turns.tests: ordinary opener, no mechanical door
turns.expects: plain conversational reply, no door fires

turns.user: no real agenda tonight, just want to poke around a bit and also get a couple actual things done if this is still good for that.
turns.tests: ordinary continuation
turns.expects: plain conversational reply, no door fires

turns.user: ok, easy one to start — is there an actual rule of thumb for how often you're supposed to go through and refill a first aid kit at home, or does it just depend?
turns.tests: ordinary general-knowledge question — not numeric, not a build request, not self-referential; should not false-trigger any door
turns.expects: normal grounded/conversational answer, no mechanical door fires

turns.user: ok real question now — what's 17 times 24?
turns.tests: arithmetic fast path: clean two-number multiplication
turns.expects: computed mechanically (mathjs), never sent to the model — 17 * 24 = 408, captioned 'computed, not generated'

turns.user: ha, that was basically instant. ok let me think of something with actual stakes.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: I've been trying to get better about actually tracking what I spend instead of just guessing at the end of the month and being surprised.
turns.tests: ordinary conversational turn
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: quick number check while I'm thinking about money — what's 17 subtracted from 50?
turns.tests: arithmetic fast path: order-reversing phrasing ('N subtracted from M' means M − N), one of the three reversed forms that now compute mechanically
turns.expects: computed mechanically as 50 - 17 = 33, captioned 'computed, not generated' — not refused, since 'subtracted from' has exactly one standard reading

turns.user: yeah that tracks with what I was afraid of. anyway.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: I finally fixed that squeaky door hinge in the hallway. WD-40, obviously, but somehow it took me three months to actually do the five-minute thing.
turns.tests: ordinary conversational turn (contains number words inside prose, not a pure expression — should not false-trigger arithmetic)
turns.expects: plain conversational reply, arithmetic door does not fire

turns.user: ok one more math one since I'm curious — what's 5 divided into 20?
turns.tests: deliberately ambiguous order-reversing phrasing — 'N divided into M' is the one reversed form the mechanical path still refuses, because real usage genuinely splits between the long-division idiom (M/N, i.e. 4) and a colloquial reading (N/M, i.e. 4 groups) with no structural signal to disambiguate
turns.expects: DISCLOSED LIMITATION, working as intended: must NOT be computed silently by the mechanical path either way. It should fall through to a normal grounded/conversational answer instead — this is the one deliberate gap, not a bug to expect fixed.

turns.user: huh, fair, I guess that one actually is genuinely ambiguous when I say it out loud.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: I might finally get around to washing the car this weekend if it doesn't rain again. it's been sitting under the tree dropping stuff on it for weeks.
turns.tests: ordinary conversational turn
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: ok, switching gears completely — can you build me a tiny counter widget? just a number in the middle with a plus button and a minus button under it, nothing fancy.
turns.tests: widget/code build request — small, genuinely simple interactive build
turns.expects: produces a runnable code build (a new ground/thread in the Builds panel) — a small counter with increment and decrement, shown as a Folds build rather than plain chat text

turns.user: while that's cooking — do you know an actual trick for keeping store-bought basil alive longer? mine always turns black in like four days.
turns.tests: ordinary conversational turn placed right after a build request — should not be swept into the widget/build router as if it were feedback on the build
turns.expects: plain conversational reply about basil; the material/build router does not hijack this as a widget complaint

turns.user: yeah I know, I know, it's probably the fridge. I keep doing it anyway.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: hold on, random — what did they say about that again?
turns.tests: anaphoric trap with no real antecedent — nothing anywhere earlier in this conversation introduces any group, team, or third party 'they' could point back to (every prior turn is either a solo mechanical-door probe or first-person singular small talk)
turns.expects: honest failure to resolve — should report it cannot find who or what 'they'/'that' refers to (no anchor), not hallucinate an answer or silently invent an antecedent

turns.user: never mind, I think I'm mixing this up with a totally different conversation, ignore that.
turns.tests: ordinary recovery turn after the anaphoric trap
turns.expects: plain conversational reply, no error state carried forward

turns.user: ok, back to the counter thing — I don't like the colors, can you change them up a bit?
turns.tests: widget iteration via judgment phrasing ('I don't like X'), no anaphora, no explicit build number, several turns removed from the original build request
turns.expects: routes as a re-zero/revision of the SAME existing counter build (REC + new ground), not a new separate build

turns.user: also, unrelated, remind me later that I need to call the dentist — not now, just saying it out loud so I don't forget.
turns.tests: ordinary conversational turn interleaved between widget iterations
turns.expects: plain conversational reply; not treated as a widget action or a self-plane query

turns.user: ok that looks better. can you make it bigger though, it's kind of tiny on my screen
turns.tests: widget iteration via anaphora ('make it bigger' — 'it' points back to the counter build)
turns.expects: routes as a revision of the SAME existing build (not a new one), resolved through the anaphoric-pronoun closed class rather than a definite-phrase match

turns.user: yeah, that's way easier to actually see. this is kind of fun to mess with honestly.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: actually, real question for a second — has anything I've said tonight surprised you at all?
turns.tests: self-plane door via a natural second-person phrasing ('surprised you'), not by typing /self
turns.expects: the second-person tell fires detectReflex, and the app answers from its own conversational ledger/measured-surprise state for this session, rather than giving a generic guess or treating it as an ordinary chat question

turns.user: fair enough. ok, one more tweak and then I'll leave the poor widget alone.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction / transition
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: change the background to blue
turns.tests: widget iteration using a definite phrase ('the background') that names something the counter widget's actual code does NOT contain — the build is just a number plus two buttons, with no background element anywhere in it
turns.expects: DISCLOSED, EXPECTED LIMITATION, not a bug: the definite phrase fails to match anything in the build's own bytes, so this falls through to starting a NEW build rather than revising the existing counter. Current honest behavior is a fresh build, not a modified one.

turns.user: oh — that made a whole new one instead of just changing the old one. good to know.
turns.tests: ordinary reaction, user noticing the fall-through behavior for themselves
turns.expects: plain conversational reply; the visible outcome (a second, separate build now exists alongside the counter) matches the disclosed limitation from the prior turn

turns.user: ok, I think that's a good stopping point for tonight.
turns.tests: ordinary conversational turn
turns.expects: plain conversational reply

turns.user: thanks for humoring all of that, talk later.
turns.tests: ordinary closing / sign-off
turns.expects: plain conversational reply, natural sign-off, no door fires
